newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen mixed to lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen mixed to lower at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open mixed to lower after a rally Friday that set record highs on the S&P 500 Index and NYSE Composite Index and left the Dow Industrials just 27 points shy of an all-time high.

"I think we are going into a mixed morning. There is nothing dramatic on the news front and bonds are waiting for the supply that will come out of the refunding this week," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "I see an unfocused day with everyone watching the dollar and waiting for the refunding on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday."
"Stocks have had a nice move, and I see them pausing here as the dollar gives up a little ground," Wachtel said.
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said tech stocks should continue to do well. He cited strength in the issues in overnight London trade.
"I think the techs, biotechs, drugs and financials will continue to outpace the market even if the Dow begins to correct because of weakness in oil stocks," he said.
Results of the weekend meeting of Group of Seven financial leaders may prove to be positive for U.S. stocks, Cardillo said.
The G7 nations were unified in their desire to arrest the dollar's rapid rise and for greater stability in currency markets.

"It is bearish news for the dollar and its strength may taper off. But (a weaker dollar) will be better for the multinational companies and would increase the possibility of our exports remaining brisk," Cardillo said.
Among special situations, Westinghouse Electric Corp said it would buy Gaylord Entertainment Co's TNN and CMT cabele networks for $1.55 billion in stock.
The long bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average rose 314.13 points, or 1.76 percent, to close at 18,181.17.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was up 21.9 points at 4329.7.
U.S. stocks were mixed to slightly firmer in London, but currency volatility limited European dealings, traders said.

Shares in Atlantic Richfield Co drew some buying interest against a generally weaker oil sector on news that ARCO was to sign a $5.2 billion joint venture pact with Russian oil giant LUKoil, dealers said.
ARCO was up 1/2 at 129.
Texaco Inc was down 3/8 to 101-3/4 while Mobil Corp was off 1/4 at 129.

Philip Morris Cos Inc firmed 3/8 to 121-1/2, buoyed by a report that British tobacco giant B.A.T Industries Plc was mulling a deal to settle U.S. tobacco suits, traders said. Investors hope Philip Morris will also settle, one traders said.
Technology shares were generally firmer. International Business Machines Corp rose 1/2 to 149-1/4, Intel Corp added 3/4 to 157-1/4, and Microsoft Corp firmed 3/8 to 100-3/4.
The dollar stalled under 123 yen in Tokyo and was calm against the yen and mark in Europe.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column says that if there is to be a transaction on Wall Street modeled on the merger of Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover, one of the likeliest candidates may be PaineWebber Group Inc.
The New York Times's Market Place column says analysts expect Time Warner Inc to report strong fourth quarter results, but few see the company's stock getting a lift from the data.
